intent: Achieve the final architectural target by removing all legacy state management infrastructure and implementing native x402 programmable settlement. Demonstrate the maximum reduction in codebase complexity and the shift to a purely synchronous, agentic payment model.
key_points: Complete removal of the legacy state manager, webhook handler, and transaction database. The system must operate with zero STATE_MGMT_LINE markers.
Native x402 settlement replaces the VirtualCardService translation layer. Payments flow directly from the agent to the merchant via x402, eliminating the intermediate virtual card issuance step.
The ElizaOS action handler is simplified to a single-path synchronous settlement. All legacy fallback and polling logic is decommissioned.
Consolidated observability: The Stage Three service aggregates metrics from Stage One and Stage Two to produce the final migration comparison report.
Maintain high aesthetic standards for the final observability dashboard, emphasizing the 100% reduction in local state complexity.
warnings: Stage Three represents a breaking change from legacy fiat merchant compatibility. It assumes a merchant ecosystem that natively accepts x402 programmable payments.
Ensure the final metrics audit is strictly verified against the Stage One and Stage Two baselines to maintain the credibility of the migration guide.
The removal of the state manager means the system has zero recovery complexity because it carries zero local state; failure handling shifts entirely to the chain/facilitator layer.
